purpose: Record bounded corrected-source re-extraction outputs for the five C2-LT-B3 source-resolution-supported issue rows before a downstream independent fresh review and artifact gate.

scope.extractionLimit: This register records corrected source-context extraction only; it does not itself create reviewed artifacts or authorize model admission.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: European Stroke Organisation and European Society for Swallowing Disorders guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of post-stroke dysphagia
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Replaces mismatched PMID 28390560 with PMID 34746431, the European Stroke Organisation and European Society for Swallowing Disorders guideline for diagnosis and treatment of post-stroke dysphagia.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Guideline article published in 2021 and indexed by PubMed; use as corrected source identity and PSD guideline-context anchor pending independent review of currentness and full recommendation details.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating post-stroke dysphagia as a continuity domain involving screening of stroke patients, dysphagia assessment for at-risk patients, swallowing-safety treatment options, nutrition/hydration risks, aspiration pneumonia, mortality and poor-outcome pathways.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include dysphagia screening coverage, dysphagia assessment after risk identification, aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition, dehydration, feeding status, swallowing physiology, swallowing safety and early mortality.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Acute stroke patients and multidisciplinary stroke-care teams managing post-stroke dysphagia; individual swallowing advice, diet orders and treatment selection remain outside this row.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: PSD can increase aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition and dehydration risk, and guideline-structured screening or assessment can define detection and transition variables for continuity protection.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: The abstract reports moderate evidence for dysphagia screening and low to moderate evidence for treatment options; intervention details, evidence grades, availability and implementation context require full guideline review.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as corrected guideline identity and endpoint vocabulary for PSD screening, assessment and management routes. Do not infer calibrated mortality reduction or individual swallowing treatment benefit.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if full guideline review cannot bind a candidate endpoint to a specific recommendation or evidence grade.
Downgrade if the row is reused outside stroke-associated dysphagia or multidisciplinary stroke care.
Block artifact promotion if screening, treatment or nutrition claims are converted into individual diet, swallowing or aspiration-risk advice.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis: Executive summary
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Replaces mismatched PMID 26494222 with PMID 27358333, the International consensus guidance for management of myasthenia gravis: Executive summary.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Consensus executive summary published in Neurology in 2016; use as corrected baseline consensus source, with newer MG updates requiring separate currentness review before being treated as current guidance.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports MG as a continuity domain involving goals of treatment, minimal manifestations, remission, ocular MG, impending crisis, manifest crisis, refractory MG, symptomatic/immunosuppressive treatment routes, IVIG/plasma exchange, thymectomy, juvenile MG, MuSK-associated MG and pregnancy-specific considerations.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include crisis-risk classification, impending-crisis route, bulbar/respiratory weakness escalation, remission/minimal-manifestation state, refractory MG, treatment-route taxonomy, thymectomy route and subtype/context labels.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Clinicians caring for patients with MG worldwide, across adult, juvenile, ocular, refractory, MuSK-associated and pregnancy contexts; individual medication or procedure decisions are excluded.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: neuromuscular-junction failure can impair ocular, bulbar, respiratory and motor function; consensus-defined crisis and treatment categories provide state and transition vocabulary.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Formal consensus uses expert panel and RAND/UCLA appropriateness methods rather than a single effect-size estimate; later guidance, local access, subtype differences and treatment risk profiles must be reviewed separately.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as corrected consensus identity and MG state/treatment-route vocabulary. Do not use as currentness proof, individual therapy advice or calibrated crisis-risk model.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if later MG guidance supersedes or materially changes a claimed route.
Downgrade if treatment classes are generalized across all MG subtypes without context.
Block model use if crisis, pregnancy, juvenile or MuSK contexts are collapsed into one undifferentiated variable.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Diagnosis and management of spinal muscular atrophy: Part 1: Recommendations for diagnosis, rehabilitation, orthopedic and nutritional care
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Splits SMA Part 1 from the wrong Part 2 PMID by replacing the Part 1 row with PMID 29290580.
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: Part 1 of the 2018 two-part update to SMA standards of care; use only for diagnosis, rehabilitation, orthopedic/spinal management, nutrition, swallowing and gastrointestinal management scope.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports SMA as a severe SMN1-related neuromuscular disorder and Part 1 scope covering diagnosis, rehabilitation, orthopedic and spinal management, nutritional care, swallowing and gastrointestinal management.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include diagnosis route, rehabilitation route, orthopedic/spinal management, nutritional management, swallowing/GI management, motor-neuron continuity and care-standard lineage.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People with spinal muscular atrophy under standard-of-care consensus context; Part 2 pulmonary and acute-care topics must remain separate.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: SMN1-related motor neuron disease affects function and survival; Part 1 defines care-domain routes for diagnosis, rehabilitation, musculoskeletal and nutritional/swallowing support.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Consensus update context does not provide calibrated intervention effects in the abstract; new therapies and evolving standards may alter currentness and expected outcomes.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as SMA Part 1 source identity and scope-specific care-domain vocabulary. Do not merge with Part 2 or infer individual standards of care.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if Part 1 and Part 2 claims are merged into a single overbroad artifact.
Downgrade if therapy-era currentness is assumed without newer guidance review.
Block model use if diagnosis, rehabilitation or nutrition variables are treated as calibrated survival effects.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Clinical Practice Guideline: Sudden Hearing Loss (Update)
extractedRows.sourceIdentityCorrection: Pairs the AAO-HNS publisher route with PMID 31369359, the PubMed companion record for Clinical Practice Guideline: Sudden Hearing Loss (Update).
extractedRows.currentnessBoundary: 2019 AAO-HNSF guideline update indexed in PubMed; use as bibliographic companion and bounded abstract-level source until publisher full content is reviewed.
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports sudden hearing loss as an urgent adult clinical continuity domain focused on distinguishing sensorineural from conductive hearing loss, identifying rare nonidiopathic SSNHL, improving diagnostic accuracy, facilitating prompt intervention, reducing unnecessary tests/imaging and improving hearing/rehabilitative outcomes.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate variables include adult sudden hearing loss presentation, SSNHL vs conductive differentiation, idiopathic SSNHL target population, diagnostic accuracy, prompt intervention route, unnecessary tests/imaging reduction, hearing outcome and rehabilitative outcome.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Adults aged 18 years or older presenting with sudden hearing loss, especially idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss; pediatric and individualized treatment decisions are excluded.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism route: prompt recognition and management of SSNHL may improve hearing recovery and quality of life; initial diagnostic differentiation determines whether therapeutic pathways are relevant.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: PubMed abstract supports scope and quality-improvement aims but not the full key action statement detail; publisher content access and full guideline review remain needed for recommendation-level artifacts.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as companion bibliographic identity, population/scope and endpoint vocabulary. Do not count as a second independent source separate from the publisher guideline and do not generate urgent-referral or treatment-window advice.
downgradeTriggers: Downgrade if full guideline content or key action statements cannot be reviewed for a recommendation-level artifact.
Downgrade if this companion record is counted as independent evidence in addition to the same publisher guideline.
Block individual urgent-referral, steroid, imaging or treatment-window advice.
